profiles.name: Gullit Eder Acevedo
profiles.description: Gullit Eder Acevedo, known as Jaguar, is an educator and street-vendor advocate associated with the Justice 8. He was arrested in December 2023 over alleged conduct at protests and detained before obtaining bail. In January 2024, a judge dismissed most charges and reduced the remaining assault charge to a misdemeanor.
profiles.finding: San Bernardino County news clips and SBC Sentinel identify Justice8 defendant. No individually verified portrait yet; newspaper PDF image inspection remains open.

profiles.name: Deep Alpesh Kumar Patel
profiles.description: Deep Alpesh Kumar Patel, 21, of Sarasota FL, called the World Jewish Congress in NYC and left a threatening voicemail (If I had a chance, I would kill every single one of you Israelis). Pleaded guilty; 6 months federal prison.
profiles.finding: DOJ complaint and WWSB case confirm identity. Hindustan Times image fetched: Getty stock photo with unrelated drug-case alt text, rejected. Adelaide drowning victim is namesake.

profiles.name: Fr. Lee Young-Chan
profiles.description:
Fr. Lee Young-Chan is a Korean Jeju Naval Base resister. Naval base resistance, Jeju.

Since 2007, the South Korean government has been constructing a major naval base on Gangjeong village, Jeju Island — a UNESCO biosphere reserve and South Korea's southernmost island. The base, designed to host U.S. and South Korean Aegis destroyers and a port-of-call for U.S. nuclear-powered aircraft carriers, is widely understood as a forward-deployment site for the U.S. military's posture against China. Local Gangjeong residents and Korean peace activists have maintained continuous nonviolent resistance at the construction gates since 2010; hundreds have been arrested and dozens have served Korean prison sentences for trespass, obstruction, and civil disobedience.
profiles.finding: Save Jeju Now identifies priest on right in Mass photograph and center in November2012 newsletter group. Jesuit source provides identity evidence; crop/quality inspection pending. Artist and Adventist namesakes rejected.

profiles.name: Lillian Pearl Ellis
profiles.description: Lillian Pearl Ellis is defendant #12 of the 61 people indicted on September 5, 2023 under the Georgia RICO Act (O.C.G.A. 16-14-4) in the Fulton County prosecution of the "Stop Cop City" / Defend the Atlanta Forest movement opposing the Atlanta Public Safety Training Center. A warrant was issued for their arrest; they were booked into the Fulton County Jail and released on bond. The sweeping indictment, condemned by civil-liberties organizations as an attack on protected protest, remains pending.
profiles.finding: Columbia-hosted RICO indictment and SaportaReport corroborate name. Historical Ellis Morgan grave and Michigan case not linked; no portrait verified.

profiles.name: Hybachi LeMar
profiles.description: Hybachi LeMar is a Chicago anarchist organizer and writer — active with the Incarcerated Workers Organizing Committee, the Black Autonomy Federation and Englewood mutual-aid projects — who came to anarchism through a letter from the South Chicago Anarchist Black Cross during more than a year in solitary confinement in an earlier imprisonment. Arrested again in May 2023, he was held in Illinois and then extradited to the Pennsylvania prison system, maxed out his sentence, and was released in 2026, returning to organizing in Chicago. He is the author of three collections of essays.
profiles.finding: KCMO ABC image visually inspected:265px two-person photograph, too small for clean usable portrait. Alternate image shows supporters with WE LOVE LEMAR banner, not verified subject. Current support campaign image has eyes intentionally blacked out; rejected. No reconstruction. Better unredacted portrait remains needed.

profiles.name: Gabriella Oropesa
profiles.description: Gabriella Victoria Oropesa, also known as Gabs, Gaby, and Gummy, was the only one of four Florida abortion-rights activists in this case to go to trial. A federal jury convicted her on December 19, 2024 of conspiracy against rights for helping plan a series of 2022 nighttime vandalism actions at three crisis-pregnancy centers after the Dobbs decision. The court sentenced her to 120 days in prison followed by three years of supervised release. The Eleventh Circuit affirmed the conviction on November 20, 2025, holding that prosecutors could use 18 U.S.C. § 241 for a conspiracy to violate rights secured by the FACE Act.
profiles.finding: DOJ appeal decision/court filings corroborate Gabriella Victoria Oropesa. BOP record is not portrait. No verified image located.

profiles.name: Bryn Taylor
profiles.description: Bryn Taylor, 26, University of Florida PhD candidate, was arraigned May 16, 2023 for allegedly battering an officer and resisting arrest with violence at a UF reproductive rights demonstration in Gainesville. Took pre-trial diversion; charges dropped 2025 after community service.
profiles.finding: CNA/NationalCatholicRegister named two-person defendant image and UF Alligator university archive are usable follow-up leads; extraction and individual identification pending.

profiles.name: Chioke Auden Fugate
profiles.description: Chioke Auden Fugate, 23, was indicted March 6, 2023 with co-defendant Duncan Andrew Small after they allegedly lit and threw two explosive devices at the former Vance Monument in downtown Asheville on July 4, 2022 as fireworks-show crowds dispersed. Pleaded guilty; sentenced to roughly 70 days.
profiles.finding: Asheville arrest reporting names suspect and police image lead; partisan reposts not accepted without original provenance/positional identity. Local police source follow-up needed.

profiles.name: Krystal Martinez-DiPippa
profiles.description: Krystal Martinez-DiPippa is a Pittsburgh activist prosecuted with her husband, Brian “Peppy” DiPippa, after an April 2023 protest against a University of Pittsburgh event featuring anti-transgender speakers. Federal agents raided their home on May 19, 2023 and detained both for several hours. After a federal indictment, Martinez-DiPippa surrendered on June 30, 2023 and was released the same day while Brian remained in pretrial detention. She later pleaded guilty to obstructing law enforcement during a civil disorder. On January 6, 2025, the court sentenced her to three years of probation, community service, and joint restitution rather than imprisonment.
profiles.finding: Govinfo case and AP sentencing corroborate identity; no individually verified portrait obtained.

profiles.name: Vienna Forrest
profiles.description: Georgia activist arrested in December 2022 during law enforcement raids on the Weelaunee forest in Atlanta. Charged with domestic terrorism, she was held for approximately two weeks in DeKalb County Jail, where she reported being misgendered by staff and was placed in solitary confinement. She was later included in the 61-person RICO indictment brought by Georgia AG Chris Carr in August 2023; those charges were dismissed December 30, 2025.
profiles.finding: Guardian activist reporting and We Came to the Forest podcast are contextual leads. Vienna woods stock images rejected as keyword collisions.

profiles.description: Jay Smith, 32, of Freeport NY, DC Nine co-defendant in the October 22, 2020 Washington Surgi-Clinic blockade. Convicted; 10 months federal prison. Pardoned by Trump January 2025.
profiles.finding: Garland9 support page and case reports identify DC activist. Reality-TV star, Christian apologist, singer and unrelated booking images rejected.

profiles.name: William Goodman
profiles.description: William Goodman, 52, of the Bronx NY, DC Nine co-defendant in the October 22, 2020 Washington Surgi-Clinic blockade. Also faced previous 2019 charges for resisting arrest at a Michigan anti-abortion protest. Convicted; 27 months federal prison. Pardoned by Trump January 2025.
profiles.finding: American Freedom Law Center and CatholicWeekly identify activist. Named post-pardon group photograph needs crop validation. Journalist, artist and historical tycoon namesakes rejected.

profiles.name: Bob Atchison
profiles.description: Vermont-based climate activist and member of Declare Emergency, a group that used disruptive highway blockades to demand that President Biden declare a national climate emergency. On October 10, 2022, Atchison was one of seven people arrested after Declare Emergency activists blocked the inner loop of Interstate 495 (the Capital Beltway) in Montgomery County, Maryland. He was charged with obstructing or hindering free passage on a public road and failing to obey a law enforcement officer, both misdemeanors. He was sentenced to 4 days in jail and 1 year of probation. A co-defendant from the same action, William Regan, received a 30-day sentence.
profiles.finding: Vermont municipal climate documents are plausible local matches but insufficient portrait evidence. Canadian racer and Kansas forester excluded.

profiles.name: Richard Timothy Hernandez
profiles.description: Richard Timothy Hernandez, age 56, was sentenced October 4, 2022 to time served on one count of destroying government property during 2020 Portland protests at ICE facilities and federal courthouses; three original counts were reduced to one under a guilty plea.
profiles.finding: DOJ Oregon press release matches name/age/case; no portrait located in initial exact-name search.

profiles.name: Chester Gallagher
profiles.description: Chester Gallagher, 73, lead defendant in the March 5, 2021 Mt. Juliet TN reproductive-health clinic blockade by 20-25 anti-abortion protesters; 11 stayed past police dispersal warning and were charged under FACE Act. Convicted; 16 months federal prison. Pardoned by Trump January 23, 2025.
profiles.finding: DOJ Tennessee complaint and reporting corroborate activist. Canadian war memorial portrait is unrelated namesake; no verified portrait yet.
